steps.notes: dN = tau*alpha*P*exp(-alpha x)/(A h nu) with documented unit conversions reproduces all 3 targets to machine precision (rel err ~4e-16); units fully specified in docstring; q not used.
Passes ONLY with q=1.602e-19; prompt's electron-charge constant is corrupted (mantissa missing). q=1.6e-19 and CODATA q both fail (see findings).

Newton inversion of 36.2 passes with q=1.602e-19 (root unique/monotonic, so initial guess immaterial). Inherits the corrupted-q defect via internal FD-integral call; tests 1-3 fail for q=1.6e-19 and CODATA q. Test 0 (boolean isclose(Ef,0,atol=0.02)) is weak alone but bundled with 3 strong tests. No cross-contamination (--isolate 4/4).

findings.evidence: Step 36.2 prompt (and problem_description_main) state: 'the electron charge is $\times 10^{-19} C$' -- the mantissa is missing (text corruption; should read '1.602\times 10^{-19}'). The constant is required: it converts the given thermal voltage 0.0259 V into k_B*T [J] inside N_c = 2(2 pi m* k_B T / h^2)^{3/2}, so n scales as q^{3/2}. Against the frozen h5 targets (9.1156e15, 3.3385e17, 1.1881e18 cm^-3) a quad-based implementation gives: q=1.602e-19 -> rel err 0 / 1.9e-16 / 0 (bit-exact, PASS); q=1.6e-19 -> rel err 1.87e-3 on all 3 tests (FAIL, 187x over np.allclose rtol=1e-5); q=1.602176634e-19 (exact CODATA) -> rel err 1.65e-4 on all 3 tests (FAIL, 16x over rtol). steptest official joint runs: review/work/36/step_36.2.py PASS; step_36.2_q1.6e-19.py FAIL; step_36.2_q1.602176634e-19.py FAIL. The solver cannot recover the required 4-digit truncation 1.602e-19 from the prompt: the value is literally absent, and even the physically exact value fails. (The q=1.602e-19 hint inside step 36.3's test 0 code is part of the eval harness, not the model-visible prompt.)
findings.suggested_fix: Repair the constant in problem_description_main and step 36.2's prompt to read 'the electron charge is $1.602\times 10^{-19}$ C' (matching the value the frozen targets encode and the q used in 36.3 test 0).

findings.evidence: Same root cause as 36.2 (the inverse function internally evaluates fermi_dirac_integral_half_polylog, so the guessed q propagates). Targets for tests 1-3 are (-0.06461044542, 0.00155821215, 0.07650960523) eV. With q=1.602e-19 my Newton inversion matches to <1e-14 rel (steptest joint PASS, 4/4). With q=1.6e-19: abs errs 5.0e-5/6.2e-5/1.2e-4 eV -> all three np.allclose FAIL (e.g. test 2: rel err 4.0e-2 vs rtol 1e-5). With exact CODATA q: abs errs 4.4e-6/5.5e-6/1.0e-5 eV -> all three FAIL (test 2 rel err 3.5e-3). steptest: step_36.3.py PASS; step_36.3_q1.6e-19.py FAIL; step_36.3_q1.602176634e-19.py FAIL. Only test 0 (assert np.isclose(Ef,0,atol=0.02)==True) is robust to the q choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix as 36.2: restore '1.602e-19 C' in the prompt text. No change needed to targets or tests once the constant is stated.

overall_assessment: Physics, units, signatures, and targets are otherwise clean and exactly reproducible: 36.1 is flawless, and a literal-reading implementation passes all three steps. The single defect is a corrupted constant: 'the electron charge is $\times 10^{-19} C$' (mantissa dropped) in the main description and step 36.2's prompt, while the frozen targets require exactly q=1.602e-19 -- the equally standard choices 1.6e-19 and the exact CODATA value both fail steps 36.2 and 36.3 under default np.allclose. As-is, 2 of 3 steps score correct solvers as wrong unless they happen to guess the authors' 4-digit truncation; restoring the '1.602' mantissa makes the whole problem fair.
